The install.sh script is a legitimate AUR package installer for the hushmic application. It downloads from the project's own GitHub upstream (github.com/Fovty/hushmic) and verifies SHA256 checksums before installation, which is good supply-chain hygiene. The script installs the application's own files — binaries, LADSPA plugins, ONNX Runtime libraries, model files, desktop entries, icons, and licenses — to standard system paths consistent with the package's stated purpose. There is no obfuscated code, no use of eval to decode hidden blobs, no reverse shells, and no exfiltration of local data such as /etc/shadow, SSH keys, or browser data. Post-install operations like icon cache refresh via gtk-update-icon-cache are standard packaging practices. The script supports both co-located and downloaded installation modes with proper checksum verification in the latter case. No evidence of injected malicious code, backdoors, or supply-chain attack indicators was found.
